chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What do you think about one who is standing at the stopping place, if he is not in a state of wudu (ablution), what should he do when he is unable to dismount? He said: “He should perform tayammum from his saddle-cloth, or his saddle, or the mane of his riding animal, for indeed there is dust in them, and then he should perform salat (prayer).”

key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: he should perform tayammum, the dry ablution used when water is unavailable or unusable
key_terms.غُبَارًا: dust, which serves as the material for tayammum
key_terms.لِبْدِهِ: his saddle-cloth or felt pad on the riding equipment
key_terms.مَعْرَفَةِ دَابَّتِهِ: the mane of his riding animal
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the state of ritual purification required for salat

ai.seo_question: How should someone perform tayammum if they cannot get down from their riding animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person who needs ritual purification but is unable to dismount from his riding animal. It permits tayammum using dust found on items such as the saddle-cloth, saddle, or the animal’s mane, showing ease in the law of taharah and salat in constrained circumstances.
